fixes.explanation: Yes. The Teacher says "…the years approach of which you will say, “I find no pleasure in them,”" (Ecclesiastes 12:1). That's what a person says about those years. It's a heavy line, so I'll just say it plainly: I think it's meant to make us listen.

That's the opposite of what the text says. The Teacher says "…the years approach of which you will say, “I find no pleasure in them,”" (Ecclesiastes 12:1). Nobody in this verse is begging for those years to last. They are years the person says have no pleasure in them.

Not in this verse. The text says "…the years approach of which you will say, “I find no pleasure in them,”" (Ecclesiastes 12:1). The Teacher had already said that youth and vigor are fleeting (Ecclesiastes 11:10). These are different years.

Right on. The silver cord is "snapped," the golden bowl is "crushed," the pitcher is "shattered" and the wheel is "broken" (Ecclesiastes 12:6). Four different things, and each one is broken. That's the thread running through the whole verse.
